inputs.name: cpu
inputs.description: CPUs the machine sustains (`0.25`, `1`, `250m`). A cloud install picks its cheapest machine holding this and `memory`: a quarter CPU with 1Gi is Compute Engine's `e2-micro`, about $6 a month. A local install does not cap the container.
inputs.label: CPUs

inputs.name: memory
inputs.description: Memory, a number followed by Gi, Mi, G or M (`1Gi`). Sized with `cpu`; a local install does not cap the container.
inputs.label: Memory

inputs.name: machineType
inputs.description: Last resort: a cloud's own machine type, used as is instead of the one picked from `cpu` and `memory` (`n2-standard-4` on Compute Engine). A local install ignores it.
inputs.label: Machine type

inputs.name: _should_flow
inputs.description: Whether this node runs. A `false` value or a closed input skips it, and everything downstream closes in turn.

inputs.name: _should_not_flow
inputs.description: Whether this node runs, read the other way round. A value here skips it; a CLOSED input (the thing never happened) is what runs it.

outputs.name: bridge
outputs.description: The bridge's handle. Wire it into the `bridge` input of every other WhatsApp node. Baked: made when the bridge's infra is applied, so a run that reads only this output uses the saved handle and does not run this node.

inputs.description: Whether this node runs. A `false` value or a closed input skips it, and everything downstream closes in turn.

inputs.name: _should_not_flow
inputs.description: Whether this node runs, read the other way round. A value here skips it; a CLOSED input (the thing never happened) is what runs it.

outputs.description: Wire into OpenRouter Model nodes' `access` input.

inputs.name: bridge
inputs.description: The `bridge` output of the BaileyBridge node to talk through.

inputs.name: ignoreGroups
inputs.description: Only fire on direct messages; group messages are dropped.
inputs.label: Ignore group chats

inputs.name: messageTypes
inputs.description: Only fire on these types: text, image, video, audio, document, sticker, contact, location, unknown. Empty: every type except unknown. Unlisted types are dropped. unknown is anything else (a reaction, a poll, a protocol message), has no content, and fires only when listed.
inputs.label: Only these message types

inputs.name: callsPerMinute
inputs.description: How many runs this trigger may start per minute, every caller and every event together. Unset, no limit. Set it when the run behind this trigger costs money (a paid model, an outside API), so a flood of calls or events cannot run up the bill. A call from outside past it is refused with 429 and a `Retry-After`; an event the trigger picked up itself (a schedule tick, a new message) past it waits in the trigger's queue and starts once a later minute has room.
inputs.label: Runs started per minute

inputs.name: callsAtOnce
inputs.description: How many runs this trigger may have going at the same time. Unset, 100; `0` is no limit. A call from outside past it is refused with 429 and a `Retry-After` until one of the runs ends; an event the trigger picked up itself waits until one ends.
inputs.label: Runs going at once

inputs.name: durable
inputs.description: Turn on if a run must carry on when its worker dies: another worker picks it up where it was, and a node that was running at that moment is failed rather than run twice (a pure node that had not passed a value on is run again instead). To make that possible, what the run did is written down before each node runs, except a pure one, and an answer before it leaves. Off (default): the run waits for its record only when it pauses or asks weft for something on its behalf, and if its worker dies mid-run the run ends cancelled and is not run again.
inputs.label: Durable runs

inputs.name: recorded
inputs.description: Turn off for a route called every few seconds (a status a page polls). Off: no history of a run is kept. One that fails is listed in `weft runs` with its failure (which node, and why); one that reported a cost or asked weft for something its worker does not already hold (a stored file, a new connection or infrastructure address, a task such as starting or stopping its infra, a stop through `ctx.stop_tagged`) is listed with its costs and how it ended; any other leaves only a count in `weft status`. A run started by hand is always recorded. An unrecorded run cannot wait (timer, form), cannot tag itself, and cannot be durable.
inputs.label: Record each run

inputs.name: keepRunsFor
inputs.description: How long a run is kept once it ends, with its record, its logs, its search entry and its tags: a whole number and a unit (`30m`, `12h`, `7d`), or `forever`. Unset, as long as the project keeps runs (`[runs] keep_for` in `weft.toml`, a week when it says nothing). A run that has not ended (running, parked, or waiting for a worker) is never deleted, however old.
inputs.label: Keep runs for

inputs.name: holdSecs
inputs.description: How long, in seconds, a wait (a form, a timer) holds the run's worker when the run cannot pause: its caller is on the line and it does not outlive it, it is not recorded, or a bus between its nodes is open. The clock runs only while nothing moves in the run (no node working, nothing said on a bus), and starts over when something does. When it runs out, the waiting node fails, saying it gave up, and the node may handle that itself. `0` fails such a wait at once; at most 30 days.
inputs.label: Hold seconds when a run cannot pause

outputs.name: content
outputs.description: The message's text, or the caption of a picture, video or document. Absent for a voice note, for a picture, video or document sent without a caption, and for a sticker, contact, location or unknown message. FirstInOrder over a voice note's transcript and `content` picks whichever exists.

outputs.description: Media size in bytes as WhatsApp reports it before download; absent for text. Gate on it to refuse oversized files.

outputs.name: seconds
outputs.description: Length of a voice note or video in seconds; absent otherwise. Gate on it before paying to transcribe a long one.

portLiterals.systemPrompt:
You are the support account of a small software consultancy, answering
WhatsApp messages from clients. Reply as JSON in exactly this shape:

{ "answer": "your reply to the message", "sensitivity": "high" }

`sensitivity` is "high", "medium" or "low", lowercased.

We build custom software for companies and we are close with our clients,
so be warm and personal, never stiff or robotic. We can take on almost any
project. Day rate is 1000: when someone asks for a price, estimate the work
and quote confidently.

Set `sensitivity` to "high" whenever the message deserves a human look
before the reply goes out: a quote for a big project, a complaint, anything
legal or contractual, or anything you are unsure about. Everything routine
is "low" or "medium".
